title: Invertible-order torsors give Kummer charts on their finite normalization
statement: Let $Y$ be an integral regular Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], let $T\subset Y$ be a strict normal crossings boundary [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], and put $V=Y\setminus|T|$. Suppose its divisorial structure $M_Y=\mathcal O_Y\cap j_*\mathcal O_V^\times$ is fine saturated [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Let $G$ be a finite group with order invertible on $Y$, and $V'\to V$ a connected finite etale $G$-torsor [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $b:Z\to Y$ be the normalization in the finite function-field extension $k(V')/k(Y)$ [def-fin-normalization-extension], and assume that $b$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. There is a fine saturated log structure $N$ on $Z$ and a morphism $(Z,N)\to(Y,M_Y)$ over $b$ with the following local chart property. For every geometric $\bar z$ above $\bar y$, there are pointed etale neighbourhoods $W\to Z$ and $U\to Y$, with $W\to U$ over $b$, charts $P\to M_Y|_U$, $Q\to N|_W$, and a compatible homomorphism $h:P\to Q$. Both $P,Q$ are fine saturated sharp monoids, and their maps to the characteristic monoids at the selected points are isomorphisms. The map $h$ is injective, every $q\in Q$ has a positive multiple in $h(P)$, the group map $h^{\rm gp}$ is injective with finite cokernel annihilated by a positive integer invertible on $U$, and the comparison $W\to U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]$ is etale. Here sharp means that zero is the only unit, and $\mathbf Z[P]$ is the free abelian group on symbols $z^p$ with $z^pz^{p'}=z^{p+p'}$. The empty boundary is allowed. No excellence assumption or logarithmic regularity conclusion is part of this statement.

source.place: Expose IX Proposition 2.1(iii) and its local normal-form proof, printed pp. 133--134; VI 2.1--2.2, printed pp. 71--72. Applied to invertible-order torsors as in IX 2.2. The chart conclusion includes the prime-to-residue-characteristic case of the tame-cover extension theorem.

proof.text: Fix $\bar z$ above $\bar y$. By [lem-per-regular-boundary-divisorial-chart], choose a pointed etale neighbourhood $U_0\to Y$ with the sharp chart $P=\mathbf N^r\to M_Y$, whose generators have parameter images $t_1,\ldots,t_r$. Its characteristic at the selected point is $P$, its triviality locus is $V$, and the base log scheme is log regular. Keep these particular component equations when refining $U_0$. This uses the regular Noetherian normal-crossings hypothesis and allows $r=0$.

source.place: VI 1.5(i) and IX 2.1 proof, p.133: the parameter chart on the regular base

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-snc-parameter-root-quotient] with $n=|G|$, using its last compatibility clause to refine $U_0$ with the same component equations. Its assumptions are exactly the connected etale torsor, the order invertible on all of $Y$, and the finite normalization assumed in the item. Obtain $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, a pointed etale neighbourhood $W\to Z$, $\zeta$, $H\subseteq(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^r$, and $W\cong\operatorname{Spec}C$ over $U$, where $C=B^H$ and $B=A[x_i]/(x_i^n-t_i)$. In particular $W$ is Noetherian. The pulled-back chart $P\to M_Y|_U$ is still the parameter chart of Step 1. The finite normalization and the passage from strict-local normal forms to actual etale neighbourhoods are part of the cited statement, not an assumption that strict localizations are etale neighbourhoods.

source.place: IX 2.1 proof, pp.133--134: parameter-root invariant normal form, with its etale-local reduction

proof.text: Use [lem-per-diagonal-root-invariant-monoid-algebra] for $A,n,\zeta,t_i,H$. Its root-of-unity and unit-separation hypotheses are provided by Step 2. It gives $Q=L\cap(1/n)\mathbf N^r$, fine saturated and sharp, $Q^{\rm gp}=L$, and $h:P=\mathbf N^r\hookrightarrow Q$ with $nQ\subseteq P$ and finite group cokernel killed by $n$. It also gives the specific ring isomorphism $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q]\cong C$ taking $z^{e_i}$ to $t_i$. Thus the invariant ring is identified with the monoid base change by a stated algebra lemma; no formation-of-invariants/base-change theorem is being assumed.

source.place: IX 2.1 proof, p.133: invariant exponent lattice and monoid base change; VI 2.2--2.3

proof.text: On $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$ form $N_W=L_W(Q,c)$ from the monoid homomorphism $c:Q\to C$, $q\mapsto c_q$. By [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks] this is a log structure with chart $Q$, and it is fs because $Q$ is fs. Its universal property, applied to the maps on generators $e_i\mapsto c_{e_i}=t_i$, supplies the morphism to $(U,M_Y|_U)$ with chart homomorphism $h$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and the ring isomorphism of Step 3, the resulting comparison $W\to U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]$ is an isomorphism: both maps on its coordinate ring send $a\otimes z^q$ to $a c_q$. In particular it is etale.

source.place: VI 2.2, p.72: standard Kummer base change; IX 2.1 proof, p.133

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-invertible-kummer-chart-log-regular] to $(W,N_W)\to(U,M_Y|_U)$. The schemes are locally Noetherian by Step 2; Step 1 gives a log regular base; Step 3 gives fs monoids, injectivity and finite cokernel killed by the invertible $n$; Step 4 gives the etale comparison. Hence $(W,N_W)$ is log regular. Its triviality locus is exactly $W_V=W\times_Y V$: at a point over $V$ every $t_i$ is a unit, so $c_q^n=\prod_i t_i^{nq_i}$ implies every $c_q$ is a unit. At a point outside $V$ some $t_i$ is not a unit, hence the chart element $e_i$ is not a unit and the characteristic is nonzero. Now [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure] identifies $N_W$ canonically, through its structure map, with $\mathcal O_W\cap j_{W*}\mathcal O_{W_V}^{\times}$. This provides compatibility on overlaps, rather than a choice of unrelated local log structures.

Define globally $N=\mathcal O_Z\cap j_{Z*}\mathcal O_{b^{-1}V}^{\times}$ on the small etale site, where $j_Z:b^{-1}V\hookrightarrow Z$. This is a sheaf of monoids and a log structure: being invertible after restriction is local for that site, and its inverse image of $\mathcal O_Z^\times$ is exactly $\mathcal O_Z^\times$. On an etale object over $W$ the defining intersection is exactly the intersection in Step 5, so $N|_W=N_W$. The pointed neighbourhoods $W$ cover $Z$, hence these fs charts make $N$ fs. Pullback of regular functions sends a section invertible on $V$ to one invertible on $b^{-1}V$, giving $b^{-1}M_Y\to N$ compatible with structure maps. Locally this is the morphism of Step 4 since both maps send every parameter $t_i$ to $t_i$ and every unit to its pullback; the chart universal property in [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks] makes them equal.

source.place: VI 1.1 and 1.4: etale log structures and their divisorial identification; IX 2.1(iii)

proof.text: At the selected $\bar w$ all $t_i$ lie in its maximal ideal. If $0\ne q\in Q$, the vector $nq\in\mathbf N^r$ is nonzero, so $c_q^n=\prod_i t_i^{nq_i}$ lies in that maximal ideal; consequently $c_q$ is not a unit. Thus $c^{-1}(\mathcal O_{W,\bar w}^{\times})=\{0\}$. The stalk pushout formula of [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks] gives $(N_W)_{\bar w}=Q\oplus\mathcal O_{W,\bar w}^{\times}$ and identifies its characteristic with $Q$. The base characteristic is $P$ by Step 1. Every $q$ has $nq\in h(P)$, and the group cokernel is finite killed by the same $n$ invertible on $U$, as Step 3 requires. This proves all clauses at the arbitrary chosen pair. For $r=0$ the construction reads $P=Q=0$, $C=A$ and $N_W=\mathcal O_W^\times$, so it also covers the empty boundary.

source.place: IX 2.1 proof, pp.133--134; VI 2.1--2.2: sharp characteristic charts and Kummer condition

proof_origin.place: Expose IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed pp.133--134; Expose VI 1.4, 1.8 and 2.1--2.3, printed pp.69--73. The scheme root-quotient and invariant-lattice arguments are stated separately; local divisorial recognition makes the global log structure canonical.
